summary: The run trace is the evidence substrate connecting platform ownership, process state, tool events, review and defect proof.

items.text: Agent Fencing makes the trace platform-owned and binds every event to the authority under which it occurred.
Process Actor supplies Task, Run, Attempt, claim and lifecycle semantics; the trace makes that path reconstructible.
Fire, Track, Review consumes the evidence envelope first and opens the raw trace only when evidence conflicts or a result is suspicious.
The Agent–Computer Interface supplies versioned operation identities, structured results, declared effects and stable evidence pointers.
Reproduce–Patch–Prove contributes the failing baseline and passing repair as a linked red/green proof envelope.
Sidecar Metadata keeps task, lifecycle, pipeline and result records beside the durable task unit while hashes prevent silent drift.
Versioned Prompt Text connects the exact instruction revision used by a run without turning a provider chat transcript into the system of record.
Trust Layer aggregates evidence envelopes across runs; this pattern defines the underlying lineage and replay contract.
